transcript.text: If you put a meeting in in the morning,
like 10:00 a.m., you've killed my whole
morning. I can't get into any kind of
deep work and then I'm going to have 2
hours and I'm going to have lunch again
and then I'm going to have other stuff
at like we don't do that. If they are
going to do something and it's quote
very urgent and they have a very strong
argument, then I put it at the very end
of my day and I book from the back
forwards. That means that if I say I
want to end my day at 5:00 or whatever,
then it means they're going to put my my
first meeting of the day at 4:00. And if
I have a second meeting that day that's
going to be from 3:00 to 4:00. And so I
still get my whole day until 3:00
uninterrupted so I can work on the
things that matter most.
